revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Captain Vega's Four Clues
revealWordProblem.text: Captain Vega's expanded treasure map uses base camp at the origin (0, 0). Her four clues are at A(4, 3), B(-5, 2), C(-3, -4), and D(2, -5), where the x-coordinate is units east (+) or west (-) and the y-coordinate is units north (+) or south (-). Question: In which quadrant does each clue land, and how do the signs of its coordinates tell you that without plotting?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: A(4, 3) is in Quadrant I because both coordinates are positive (+, +) — east and north. B(-5, 2) is in Quadrant II because x is negative and y is positive (-, +) — west and north. C(-3, -4) is in Quadrant III because both are negative (-, -) — west and south. D(2, -5) is in Quadrant IV because x is positive and y is negative (+, -) — east and south.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do you plot points in all four quadrants?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: The signs of (x, y) tell you the quadrant: (+,+) is I, (-,+) is II, (-,-) is III, (+,-) is IV — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

onLevel.stem: Point A is at (-5, 3). If you move 8 units to the right, what are the new coordinates?
onLevel.explanation: Moving right means adding to the x-coordinate: -5 + 8 = 3. The y stays the same. New point: (3, 3).
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Moving right means adding to the x-coordinate: -5 + 8 = ___.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Moving right changes ONLY the x-coordinate. The y-coordinate stays at 3.
Add the move to the x-value: take -5 and count up 8. Careful crossing zero — use a number line if it helps.
Start at -5 and count 8 steps right: -4, -3, -2, ... keep going all 8 steps. Then keep the y as 3.
onLevel.stemEs: El punto A está en (-5, 3). Si te mueves 8 unidades a la derecha, ¿cuáles son las nuevas coordenadas?
onLevel.explanationEs: Moverse a la derecha significa sumar a la coordenada x: -5 + 8 = 3. La y se queda igual. Punto nuevo: (3, 3).
hintsEs: Moverse a la derecha cambia SOLO la coordenada x. La coordenada y se queda en 3.
Suma el movimiento al valor de x: toma −5 y cuenta 8 hacia arriba. Cuidado al cruzar el cero; usa una recta numérica si ayuda.
Empieza en −5 y cuenta 8 pasos a la derecha: −4, −3, −2, … sigue los 8 pasos. Luego conserva la y como 3.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Name the quadrant for the point (6, -1).

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: I'll read the coordinates as (y, x), so I treat this like (-1, 6): the first number -1 is negative (left) and the second number 6 is positive (up).
workedExample.workEs: Leeré las coordenadas como (y, x), así que lo trato como (-1, 6): el primer número -1 es negativo (izquierda) y el segundo número 6 es positivo (arriba).

onLevel.correctWork: The order was reversed. In an ordered pair (x, y), x ALWAYS comes first. Here x = 6 (positive → right) and y = -1 (negative → down). Right and down is Quadrant IV, not Quadrant II.
hints: In (6, -1), which number is the x-coordinate — the first or the second?
x = 6 (positive → right) and y = -1 (negative → down). Right and down land you in which quadrant?
onLevel.explanation: An ordered pair is always (x, y), so the first number is the horizontal move and the order cannot be swapped. Here x = 6 sends you right and y = -1 sends you down, which is the bottom-right region — Quadrant IV. Reading it as (-1, 6) described a completely different point.
onLevel.explanationEs: Un par ordenado siempre es (x, y), así que el primer número es el movimiento horizontal y el orden no se puede intercambiar. Aquí x = 6 te manda a la derecha y y = -1 te manda hacia abajo, que es la región inferior derecha: el Cuadrante IV. Leerlo como (-1, 6) describía un punto completamente distinto.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El orden se invirtió. En un par ordenado (x, y), la x SIEMPRE va primero. Aquí x = 6 (positiva → derecha) y y = -1 (negativa → abajo). Derecha y abajo es el Cuadrante IV, no el II.
hintsEs: En (6, -1), ¿cuál número es la coordenada x — el primero o el segundo?
x = 6 (positiva → derecha) y y = -1 (negativa → abajo). A la derecha y hacia abajo caes en ¿cuál cuadrante?

onLevel.stem: In which quadrant is the point (-3, 5)?
onLevel.explanation: Negative x with positive y places the point in Quadrant II.
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I is where x is positive and y is positive. Check the sign of each coordinate in the point and match both.
Quadrant III requires both coordinates to be negative, but 5 is positive.
Quadrant IV needs a positive x-coordinate, and here x is −3.
hints: Check the signs: x = -3 is negative and y = 5 is positive.
Negative x means left of the y-axis; positive y means above the x-axis. Which quadrant is up-and-left?
From the origin move left 3, then up 5. Count quadrants counterclockwise from top-right to name where you land.
onLevel.explanationEs: Una x negativa con una y positiva coloca el punto en el cuadrante II.
hintsEs: Revisa los signos: x = −3 es negativo y y = 5 es positivo.
Una x negativa significa a la izquierda del eje y; una y positiva significa arriba del eje x. ¿Qué cuadrante es arriba y a la izquierda?
Desde el origen muévete 3 a la izquierda y luego 5 hacia arriba. Cuenta los cuadrantes en sentido antihorario desde arriba a la derecha para nombrar dónde caes.

onLevel.stem: What are the coordinates of a point 4 units right and 2 units down from the origin?
onLevel.explanation: Right is +x and down is -y, so the point is (4, -2).
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you changed the sign of both coordinates. Instead: Right is +x and down is -y, so the point is ___.
The two coordinates are swapped. The first number always describes the horizontal move and the second the vertical move.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Two moves: right 4 (horizontal) and down 2 (vertical). Down means a NEGATIVE y.
Build (x, y): x is the right/left amount with its sign, y is the up/down amount with its sign.
Right 4 gives x = 4 (positive). Now write 'down 2' as a signed y-value and put the two in order.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Cuáles son las coordenadas de un punto que está 4 unidades a la derecha y 2 unidades hacia abajo desde el origen?
onLevel.explanationEs: A la derecha es +x y hacia abajo es -y, así que el punto es (4, -2).
hintsEs: Dos movimientos: derecha 4 (horizontal) y abajo 2 (vertical). Abajo significa una y NEGATIVA.
Arma (x, y): x es la cantidad derecha/izquierda con su signo y y es la cantidad arriba/abajo con su signo.
Derecha 4 da x = 4 (positivo). Ahora escribe 'abajo 2' como un valor de y con signo y pon los dos en orden.

extending.label: Plot one point in each quadrant: (3, 2), (-4, 1), (-2, -3), (5, -4)
extending.hint: Plot each point by moving right first, then up from the origin.
hints: Signs steer you: positive x goes right, negative x goes left, positive y goes up, negative y goes down.
For each point, do the x move first (left/right), then the y move (up/down). The label tells you which quadrant to expect.
Plot (3, 2) first: right 3, up 2 — the top-right region. Then (-4, 1): LEFT 4, then up 1.
extending.explanation: Each point starts at the origin, moves along x first and then along y, and the pair of signs tells you which region you end in. (3, 2) goes right and up to Quadrant I, (-4, 1) goes left and up to Quadrant II, (-2, -3) goes left and down to Quadrant III, and (5, -4) goes right and down to Quadrant IV.
extending.explanationEs: Cada punto empieza en el origen, se mueve primero en x y luego en y, y la pareja de signos te dice en qué región terminas. (3, 2) va a la derecha y hacia arriba, al Cuadrante I; (-4, 1) va a la izquierda y hacia arriba, al Cuadrante II; (-2, -3) va a la izquierda y hacia abajo, al Cuadrante III; y (5, -4) va a la derecha y hacia abajo, al Cuadrante IV.
hintsEs: Los signos te guían: x positiva va a la derecha, x negativa a la izquierda, y positiva sube, y negativa baja.
Para cada punto, haz primero el movimiento en x (izquierda/derecha) y luego el de y (arriba/abajo). La etiqueta te dice qué cuadrante esperar.
Ubica (3, 2) primero: derecha 3, arriba 2 — la región superior derecha. Luego (-4, 1): IZQUIERDA 4 y luego arriba 1.

extending.instructions: For each ordered pair, write the signs of x and y and name the quadrant (or axis).
extending.hint: For each point, write the sign of x and y, then name the quadrant or axis.
hints: Each row asks for the sign of x, the sign of y, then the quadrant those signs give — or an axis if a coordinate is 0.
Sign map: (+, +) I, (-, +) II, (-, -) III, (+, -) IV. A 0 for x means y-axis; a 0 for y means x-axis.
Row 1: decide if 6 is positive or negative, then -2. Write both signs, then look the pair up on the sign map.
extending.explanation: Write each coordinate's sign, then read the pair off the map: (6, -2) is (+, -) so Quadrant IV, (-3, -5) is (-, -) so Quadrant III, and (-1, 8) is (-, +) so Quadrant II. A zero means the point sits on an axis instead of inside a quadrant — (0, 7) is on the y-axis and (4, 0) is on the x-axis.
extending.explanationEs: Escribe el signo de cada coordenada y luego busca la pareja en el mapa: (6, -2) es (+, -), así que Cuadrante IV; (-3, -5) es (-, -), así que Cuadrante III; y (-1, 8) es (-, +), así que Cuadrante II. Un cero significa que el punto está sobre un eje y no dentro de un cuadrante: (0, 7) está en el eje y y (4, 0) está en el eje x.
extending.instructionsEs: Para cada par ordenado, escribe los signos de x y y, y nombra el cuadrante (o el eje).
hintsEs: Cada fila pide el signo de x, el signo de y y luego el cuadrante que dan esos signos, o un eje si una coordenada es 0.
Mapa de signos: (+, +) I, (−, +) II, (−, −) III, (+, −) IV. Un 0 en x significa eje y; un 0 en y significa eje x.
Fila 1: decide si 6 es positivo o negativo y luego −2. Escribe ambos signos y luego busca la pareja en el mapa de signos.

extending.title: Find the Quadrant Error

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: The x is -3, so I go left 3. The y is -5, so I go up 5.
workedExample.workEs: La x es -3, así que voy 3 a la izquierda. La y es -5, así que subo 5.

extending.correctWork: A negative y-coordinate means DOWN, not up. Go left 3 and DOWN 5. The point (-3, -5) is in Quadrant III (both negative), not Quadrant II.
hints: What direction does a NEGATIVE y-coordinate go — up or down?
Both coordinates are negative. In which quadrant are both x and y negative?
extending.explanation: A negative y-coordinate means down, not up. From the origin you go left 3 and DOWN 5, landing in the bottom-left region. Both coordinates are negative, and (-, -) is Quadrant III, not Quadrant II.
extending.explanationEs: Una coordenada y negativa significa hacia abajo, no hacia arriba. Desde el origen te mueves 3 a la izquierda y 5 hacia ABAJO, y caes en la región inferior izquierda. Las dos coordenadas son negativas, y (-, -) es el Cuadrante III, no el Cuadrante II.
extending.correctWorkEs: Una coordenada y negativa significa hacia ABAJO, no hacia arriba. Ve 3 a la izquierda y 5 hacia ABAJO. El punto (-3, -5) está en el Cuadrante III (ambas negativas), no en el II.
hintsEs: ¿En qué dirección va una coordenada y NEGATIVA — hacia arriba o hacia abajo?
Ambas coordenadas son negativas. ¿En cuál cuadrante x e y son negativas?

extending.prompt: A point starts in Quadrant I at (4, 6). Describe a move that puts it in Quadrant III. What must happen to both coordinates? Can you give the exact new coordinates after your move?
extending.sentenceFrame: To move from Quadrant I to Quadrant III, both coordinates must become ___. Starting at (4, 6), I could move ___ units left and ___ units down to reach (___,___), which is in Quadrant III because ___.
extending.hint: Use examples with specific coordinates to explain your thinking.
hints: Quadrant III is the bottom-left region — think about what must be true of BOTH signs there.
Plan moves that flip each sign: enough LEFT to push x = 4 below zero, enough DOWN to push y = 6 below zero.
Try moving left MORE than 4 units — say how far x = 4 travels and where it lands. Then plan the down move for y = 6.
extending.explanation: Quadrant III is the bottom-left region, so both coordinates have to end up negative. Starting at (4, 6), you need to move more than 4 units left to push x below 0 and more than 6 units down to push y below 0. Moving 6 left and 8 down, for example, lands on (-2, -2), which is Quadrant III because x and y are both negative.
extending.explanationEs: El Cuadrante III es la región inferior izquierda, así que las dos coordenadas deben terminar negativas. Empezando en (4, 6), necesitas moverte más de 4 unidades a la izquierda para llevar x por debajo de 0 y más de 6 unidades hacia abajo para llevar y por debajo de 0. Por ejemplo, moverte 6 a la izquierda y 8 hacia abajo cae en (-2, -2), que está en el Cuadrante III porque x y y son negativas.
extending.promptEs: Un punto empieza en el cuadrante I en (4, 6). Describe un movimiento que lo lleve al cuadrante III. ¿Qué debe pasar con las dos coordenadas? ¿Puedes dar las coordenadas nuevas exactas después de tu movimiento?
hintsEs: El Cuadrante III es la región de abajo a la izquierda: piensa qué debe cumplirse con AMBOS signos ahí.
Planea movimientos que cambien cada signo: suficiente IZQUIERDA para que x = 4 baje de cero y suficiente ABAJO para que y = 6 baje de cero.
Prueba moverte MÁS de 4 unidades a la izquierda: di cuánto viaja x = 4 y dónde cae. Luego planea el movimiento hacia abajo para y = 6.

extending.stem: A point (a, b) has a < 0 and b < 0. In which quadrant does it lie?
extending.explanation: Both coordinates negative places the point in Quadrant III.
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I is where x is positive and y is positive. Check the sign of each coordinate in the point and match both.
Quadrant II has a negative x but a positive y, and here b is negative too.
Quadrant IV pairs a positive x with a negative y, but a is negative here.
hints: a < 0 means the x is negative; b < 0 means the y is negative — this is a signs question in disguise.
Negative x goes left and negative y goes down. Find the down-and-left region, counting I–IV counterclockwise.
Pick a sample like (-2, -3) and plot it: left 2, down 3. Which region did you land in?
extending.stemEs: Un punto (a, b) tiene a < 0 y b < 0. ¿En qué cuadrante se encuentra?
extending.explanationEs: Tener las dos coordenadas negativas coloca el punto en el cuadrante III.
hintsEs: a < 0 significa que la x es negativa; b < 0 significa que la y es negativa — esta es una pregunta de signos disfrazada.
Una x negativa va a la izquierda y una y negativa va hacia abajo. Halla la región de abajo a la izquierda, contando I–IV en sentido contrario a las manecillas del reloj.
Escoge un ejemplo como (-2, -3) y ubícalo: 2 a la izquierda, 3 hacia abajo. ¿En qué región caíste?

extending.stem: Reflecting the point (3, -6) across the x-axis gives which point?
extending.explanation: Reflecting across the x-axis negates the y-coordinate: (3, -6) → (3, 6).
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you changed the sign of both coordinates — re-read what the question is asking for.
Both coordinates changed sign, which is a reflection across both axes. A reflection across the x-axis leaves the x-coordinate alone.
You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.

extending.stemEs: Reflejar el punto (3, -6) sobre el eje x da como resultado ¿cuál punto?
extending.explanationEs: Reflejar sobre el eje x cambia el signo de la coordenada y: (3, -6) → (3, 6).
hintsEs: Reflejar sobre el eje x voltea el punto verticalmente: cambia arriba/abajo, no izquierda/derecha.
La coordenada x se queda igual; la coordenada y cambia de signo. No intercambies el orden de los dos números.

extending.stem: A sonar ping locates an enemy submarine at (-5, -2). In which quadrant should Captain Vega aim her shot?
extending.explanation: A negative x means left and a negative y means down, so (-5, -2) is in Quadrant III, where both coordinates are negative.
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I is where x is positive and y is positive. Check the sign of each coordinate in the point and match both.
Quadrant II sits above the x-axis, so its y-coordinate is positive, but this ping's y is −2.
Quadrant IV needs a positive x-coordinate, and this ping's x is −5.
extending.stemEs: Un eco de sonar ubica un submarino enemigo en (-5, -2). ¿En qué cuadrante debe apuntar su disparo la capitana Vega?
extending.explanationEs: Una x negativa significa izquierda y una y negativa significa abajo, así que (-5, -2) está en el cuadrante III, donde las dos coordenadas son negativas.
hints: The signs of the two coordinates decide the quadrant: x tells left or right, and y tells up or down.
Check each sign separately, then find the corner of the plane that matches both directions.
In (−5, −2) the x is negative, so move left of the origin; the y is negative, so move down. Name the quadrant those two moves land in.
hintsEs: Los signos de las dos coordenadas deciden el cuadrante: la x indica izquierda o derecha y la y indica arriba o abajo.
Revisa cada signo por separado y después busca la esquina del plano que coincide con las dos direcciones.
En (−5, −2) la x es negativa, así que muévete a la izquierda del origen; la y es negativa, así que muévete hacia abajo. Nombra el cuadrante donde caen esos dos movimientos.

extending.stem: Captain Vega's lookout reports a ship in Quadrant II. What signs will its coordinates (x, y) have?
extending.explanation: Quadrant II is up and to the left of the origin, so x is negative and y is positive: (-, +).
choiceFeedback: That is the sign pair for Quadrant I. Find the named quadrant on the grid, then read whether x sits left or right of the origin and whether y sits above or below it.
Two negative signs place a point below and to the left of the origin. Quadrant II sits above the x-axis.
That pairing puts a point to the right of and below the origin. Check which side of the y-axis Quadrant II is on.
extending.stemEs: El vigía de la capitana Vega reporta un barco en el cuadrante II. ¿Qué signos tendrán sus coordenadas (x, y)?
extending.explanationEs: El cuadrante II está arriba y a la izquierda del origen, así que la x es negativa y la y es positiva: (-, +).
hints: Quadrants are numbered counterclockwise, starting from the top-right corner.
Picture where Quadrant II sits relative to the origin, then read off the horizontal and vertical directions.

hintsEs: Los cuadrantes se numeran en sentido contrario a las manecillas del reloj, empezando por la esquina superior derecha.
Imagina dónde queda el cuadrante II respecto al origen y después identifica las direcciones horizontal y vertical.
El cuadrante II está arriba del eje x, así que la y es positiva. Decide qué signo debe tener la x para un punto del lado izquierdo del plano.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants is matching each sign to the wrong axis — for example, seeing (-2, 5) and thinking "the x is negative so I move DOWN, and the y is positive so I move RIGHT," which lands the point in Quadrant IV. But the x-coordinate always controls left/right, never up/down: negative x means LEFT (not down), and positive y means UP (not right). So (-2, 5) is actually left 2, up 5 — Quadrant II. Before you submit, check that you used the x-coordinate for left/right and the y-coordinate for up/down, and never swapped them.

diagram.title: City Map: Four-Quadrant Locations
diagram.caption: City Hall sits at the origin; read each point's signs to see its quadrant — Library (-,+) is II, School (+,+) is I, Park (+,-) is IV, Hospital (-,-) is III.

connect.scenario: A city uses a coordinate grid to map locations. City Hall is at the origin (0, 0). The library is at (-3, 4), the park is at (5, -2), the school is at (2, 3), and the hospital is at (-4, -1).
connect.promptQuestion: How do four-quadrant coordinates help a city map locations in every direction from the center?
connect.prompt: The library is in Quadrant ___ because its x is ___ and its y is ___. The park is in Quadrant ___ because ___. Four-quadrant coordinates help because ___.

check.stem: Which quadrant is the library (−3, 4) in?
check.explanation: x is negative (left of center) and y is positive (above center). That is the upper-left region — Quadrant II.

check.stem: Which quadrant is the park (5, −2) in?
check.explanation: x is positive (right) and y is negative (below). That is the lower-right region — Quadrant IV.

check.stem: Which location is in Quadrant III?
check.explanation: Quadrant III is where BOTH coordinates are negative — the lower-left region. The hospital at (−4, −1) is the only one.

connect.modelAnswer: Read the signs to find the quadrant. Library (−3, 4): x negative, y positive → Quadrant II. Park (5, −2): x positive, y negative → Quadrant IV. The school (2, 3) is Quadrant I and the hospital (−4, −1) is Quadrant III. Four quadrants let the city map locations in every direction from City Hall at the origin, instead of only up and to the right.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — A point has a negative x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Which quadrant is it in?
exitTicket.explanation: Quadrant III is where both x and y are negative. This means the point is left of the origin and below the origin.
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I has both positive — you need both negative.
Quadrant II has negative x but positive y — check the y sign.
Quadrant IV has positive x — you need x negative too.
hints: Negative x and negative y — think about which direction each sign pushes the point.
Negative x means LEFT of the y-axis; negative y means BELOW the x-axis. Find the region that is both.
Plot a sample like (-4, -5): left 4, down 5. Count quadrants counterclockwise from top-right to name it.

questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 4) and (1, 4). How long is the bottom side?
questions.explanation: The bottom side runs from x = 1 to x = 7 at the same height: 7 − 1 = 6 units.

questions.stem: Using that same rectangle — (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 4), (1, 4) — what is its area?
questions.explanation: The sides are 6 units and 3 units, so the area is 6 × 3 = 18 square units.

questions.stem: A square has vertices (−2, −2), (2, −2), (2, 2) and (−2, 2). What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Each side is |−2| + |2| = 4 units, and 4 × 4 = 16 units around.

questions.stem: Three vertices of a rectangle are (0, 0), (5, 0) and (5, 3). What is the fourth vertex?
questions.explanation: The fourth corner lines up above (0, 0) and across from (5, 3), so it is (0, 3).
